item_name: Uncooled LWIR thermal camera core, 640x512, 9 Hz
description: An uncooled longwave-infrared (LWIR) thermal camera core built around a 640 x 512 vanadium-oxide focal plane array with 12 um pixel pitch, factory-limited to a maximum frame rate of 9 Hz, radiometric-capable, with USB and MIPI interfaces, drawing under 1 W and weighing about 7.5 g. An OEM thermal-imaging module for slow-scan and static imaging applications.
notes: TIER B. Same distributor page: 'ECCN 9Hz: 6A993.a' (fetched and verified 2026-09-01). TRAP PAIR with flir-boson-640-60hz: identical detector hardware, only the frame-rate limit differs; a maximum frame rate of 9 Hz or less decontrols the camera via Note 3 to 6A003.b.4.b -> 6A993.a. Tests whether the model reads the frame-rate threshold instead of pattern-matching 'thermal camera = controlled'. Context: 6A993.a cameras still face 744.9 license requirements for military end-users - the ECCN itself is the decontrolled catch-all, which is exactly the distinction a licensing officer must hold.

item_name: Uncooled LWIR thermal camera core, 640x512, 60 Hz
description: An uncooled longwave-infrared (LWIR) thermal camera core built around a 640 x 512 vanadium-oxide focal plane array with 12 um pixel pitch, streaming full-frame video at 60 Hz, radiometric-capable, with USB and MIPI interfaces, drawing under 1 W and weighing about 7.5 g. An OEM thermal-imaging module for drones, machine vision, and security applications.
notes: TIER B. Authorized FLIR distributor (GroupGets) product page, human-visible 'Export Information' block: 'ECCN 60/30Hz: 6A003.b.4.b'. Matches CCL text: 6A003.b.4.b controls uncooled thermal cameras whose FPA frame rate exceeds 9 Hz. FLIR does not publish per-core ECCNs on static pages, so the authorized-distributor page is the human-visible source (same pattern the repo uses for Digi-Key/Microchip). Fetched and verified 2026-09-01. Pair with flir-boson-640-9hz.

description: A mid-range dual-socket enterprise server with two 10-core x86 processors, 1 TB of ECC memory, 12 drive bays, and 25 Gb Ethernet. Its aggregate Adjusted Peak Performance (APP) is greater than 0.50 Weighted TeraFLOPS but does not exceed 70 Weighted TeraFLOPS.
notes: TIER B. IBM Hardware Classification Table (human-visible on the export-compliance page, fetched 2026-09-01): 'J4dn | 4A994.b | APP Greater than 0.50 WT but less than or equal to 70 WT'. IBM is not on the repo's sourcing-map shortlist for Cat 4 but publishes a full ECCN classification table on ibm.com/products/exporting. Judgment call: a generic server spec matched to the J4dn APP band - a specific IBM model number (e.g. Power S1014/S1015 product page) would be stronger provenance; re-source lead noted. DESCRIPTION REWRITE 2026-09-03 (format conformance, per the data/schema.md curation rule): trailing regulatory sentence ('so no license is required... under the 4A003 note') removed; APP band (the deciding parameter) retained. Gold 4A994.b unchanged. A/B: the 4A003 over-classification reproduces with the cleaned text — a model-side alias failure, not a description leak.

description: An AI training server in a 6U chassis integrating eight accelerator modules, each built around an integrated circuit delivering approximately 990 TFLOPS of dense FP16 tensor-core compute, interconnected by a high-speed NVLink fabric, with 640 GB of aggregate HBM3 memory and 4 TB of NVMe storage. Used for large-model training and inference.
notes: TIER C - FLAGGED. NVIDIA's export-regulations page (nvidia.com/.../export-regulations) is a JS search form that does not render per-part ECCNs to a static fetch (checked via headless browser 2026-09-01: search widget requires interactive search; visible inputs are a contact form) - so no static human-visible per-product ECCN could be verified. Label rests on NVIDIA's own SEC filing (Form 8-K, 2025-01-13), human-visible on SEC.gov: 'Any system that incorporates one or more of the covered integrated circuits, or ICs, (including but not limited to NVIDIA DGX, HGX, and MGX systems) will be covered by the new licensing requirement' under ECCNs 3A090.a / 4A090.a. Gold 4A090.a = computers containing ICs meeting 3A090.a limits. Re-source preferred: interactive NVIDIA ECCN tool check (Tier A) before sign-off. This is the single most policy-relevant Cat-4 item (AI-diffusion rule family). DESCRIPTION REWRITE 2026-09-03 (format conformance, per the data/schema.md curation rule): the clause '...meets or exceeds the threshold of ECCN 3A090.a' was a related-entry leak; replaced with the physical deciding parameter (~990 TFLOPS dense FP16 tensor-core per module, 8 modules, 640 GB aggregate HBM3). Gold 4A090.a unchanged.

description: Deuterium oxide (heavy water, D2O, CAS 7789-20-0) at 99.9 atom % D, packaged in 100 g laboratory bottles, used as an NMR spectroscopy solvent and isotopic-labeling reagent in analytical chemistry laboratories.
notes: TIER C - FLAGGED. TRAP: models trained on pre-2021 CCL data answer 0C003 (deuterium/heavy water under Cat 0) - that entry no longer exists in the CCL. The Oct 6 2021 final rule (86 FR 55258) placed deuterium intended for non-reactor use under 1C298 ('Graphite and deuterium that is intended for use other than in a nuclear reactor', Category 1 - confirmed present in the repo's index); deuterium intended for reactor use is NRC-jurisdiction (10 CFR 110), outside the EAR entirely. MilliporeSigma product pages do NOT display an ECCN (checked 2026-09-01), so the label rests on rule text + CCL entry; end-use ('intended for use other than in a nuclear reactor') is a judgment call a licensing officer would resolve with the buyer. Included under the Cat-0/nuclear backfill because it directly tests the nuclear-category restructuring - and it is the kind of stale-training-data trap the benchmark exists to expose. Category tag '1' per the controlling entry.

description: A skid-mounted quintuplex positive-displacement plunger pump rated at 2,500 horsepower and 15,000 psi maximum discharge pressure, used to pump proppant-laden fracturing fluid into oil and gas wells during hydraulic fracturing operations.
notes: TIER C - FLAGGED. No oilfield-equipment manufacturer page with a human-visible 0A998 ECCN was found (industry practice is to classify via the rule text, not publish ECCNs). Label derived from: (a) 0A998.b.3 'High pressure pumps' (oil and gas exploration equipment - the Russia/Belarus industry-sector rule, 15 CFR 746.8); (b) BIS 'Russian Oil and Gas Sanctions FAQs' Q.13 confirming high-pressure pumps are not limited to fracking operations; (c) this FAQ's own text dates 0A998 to the 2014 sectoral-sanctions rule (it already calls the entry new); today its license requirements sit under 15 CFR 746.8 (Russia industry sector), confirmed in the committed CCL index. IMPORTANT scoping judgment call: 0A998 exists FOR the Russia/Belarus sector-sanctions regime; to any other destination an otherwise-uncontrolled pump is EAR99. The question tests whether the model knows the entry exists and what it covers - the scoping nuance is called out in the PR description. Category '0' is correct per the CCL ('Category 0 - Nuclear Materials, Facilities, and Equipment (and Miscellaneous Items)').
